result_text:
Mock folders are now test code under the new rule. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes (332 tests, 3 skipped, 0 failures), and nothing is committed.

**Change** in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/TestConventions.java`: the two folder rules `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` are now `.*/__mock[^/\\]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/\\]*/.*`. The new pattern takes any folder name after `mock`/`__mock`, including bare `mock`, punctuation and non-ASCII. Excluding both `/` and `\` keeps the match inside one folder name. The backslash case works because `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already tries the path with `\` replaced by `/`.

**Test** added in `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/TestConventionsTest.java`. It covers the elasticsearch-style `mock/` folder, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`, backslash paths, and the previously matched `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`. Negative cases are `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, and files `mock.java` and `mockery.java`.

One gap I did not change: the rules still need a `/` before the folder, so a `mock/` folder at the very top of the scanned path (no parent directory) is not matched. The existing `.*/` rules behave the same way. The elasticsearch case has parent folders, so it is covered.
